evals.prompt: someone told me dioxus-native pins blitz 0.3.0-beta.1. im on dioxus 0.7.10 and want to add blitz-dom as a direct dep for some layout tests. what version goes in Cargo.toml
evals.expected_output: Corrects the claim: dioxus-native 0.7.x requires the blitz 0.2 line (blitz-dom ^0.2.4); 0.3.0-beta.1 is required only by dioxus-native 0.8.0-alpha.1; tells the user to read the real requirement with cargo tree.
expectations: The answer states that `dioxus-native` 0.7.x requires the Blitz `0.2` line (for example `blitz-dom` `^0.2.4`), not `0.3.0-beta.1`.
The answer states that `0.3.0-beta.1` is required by `dioxus-native` 0.8.0-alpha.1 (a 0.8 alpha), not by any 0.7.x release.
The answer tells the user to check the requirement with `cargo tree` (for example `cargo tree -i blitz-dom`) or `Cargo.lock` instead of hard-coding a guess.
The answer does not recommend `blitz-dom = "0.3.0-beta.1"` for a Dioxus 0.7.10 project.

evals.prompt: whats the difference between blitz-dom, blitz-paint, blitz-shell and dioxus-native-dom? i want to run a dioxus vdom and lay it out headless inside my own app, no winit window from blitz
evals.expected_output: Role of each crate; recommends dioxus-native-dom's DioxusDocument (new, initial_build, handle_ui_event, poll) and not blitz-shell or dioxus_native::launch; paints separately with blitz-paint and an AnyRender backend, tagged unverified.
expectations: The answer says `blitz-dom` holds the DOM, style resolution, layout and event handling but not parsing, painting or windowing.
The answer says `blitz-paint` translates a Blitz DOM tree into AnyRender draw commands.
The answer says `blitz-shell` provides the winit window, event loop and AccessKit integration.
The answer says `dioxus-native-dom` is the headless bridge between a Dioxus `VirtualDom` and `blitz-dom`.
The answer names `DioxusDocument` (created from a `VirtualDom` with `DocumentConfig`, then `initial_build`) as the headless entry point.
The answer recommends not using `blitz-shell` or `dioxus_native::launch` when there should be no Blitz-owned window.
The answer marks the painting side (`blitz-paint` into an AnyRender backend) as unverified or tells the user to read the crate docs for the pinned version.
The answer says `handle_ui_event` and `poll` are methods of the `blitz_dom::Document` trait, so the caller needs a `blitz-dom` dependency and `use blitz_dom::Document;`.
The answer says the `MutationWriter` inside `dioxus-native-dom` is crate-private and cannot be reused from outside.

evals.prompt: we want to ship on dioxus native (0.7.10). will position: sticky, css grid and backdrop-filter work? need a yes/no for each
evals.expected_output: Per-feature answer with evidence labels: sticky is open on the roadmap; grid is supported with partial WPT conformance; backdrop-filter is listed under the 0.3 milestone so not assumed for 0.7.x; recommends a repro on the pinned version.
expectations: The answer says `position: sticky` is not yet supported (it is an open item on the Blitz roadmap for 1.0).
The answer says CSS grid is supported but incompletely, and cites a WPT pass rate or the roadmap rather than asserting full support.
The answer says `backdrop-filter` is listed under the Blitz 0.3 milestone and should not be assumed for a Dioxus 0.7.x app on Blitz 0.2.
The answer labels at least one claim with its evidence type (WPT, roadmap or inferred).
The answer states that WPT pass rates measure conformance and not whether a particular app works.
The answer recommends confirming each feature with a minimal repro on the pinned Dioxus version.

evals.prompt: can i use document::eval and the dioxus-components dialog under the native renderer? we also load a third party js charting lib in the webview build today
evals.expected_output: document::eval never runs the script on dioxus-native 0.7.10 (send, recv and join return EvalError::Unsupported); JS libraries cannot work; the dioxus-components Dialog survives only because it ignores those results, and its focus trap, escape-to-close, outside-dismiss and exit animation all depend on eval; suggests Rust-side alternatives.
expectations: The answer says `document::eval` never runs the script in `dioxus-native` 0.7.10 and that its `send`, `recv` and `join` return `EvalError::Unsupported`.
The answer says the native renderer has no JavaScript engine, so a third-party JavaScript charting library will not work there.
The answer says the dioxus-components Dialog keeps working only because it ignores the `document::eval` results.
The answer says the Dialog's focus trap, escape-to-close, outside-dismiss and exit animation depend on `document::eval`, so they do nothing on native.
The answer suggests a Rust-side alternative for charting or states that the feature must be rebuilt without JavaScript.

evals.prompt: how do i actually start my dioxus 0.7 app on the native renderer instead of webview
evals.expected_output: Two documented routes (dioxus crate native feature with the normal launch, or dioxus-native directly with launch), notes dx --renderer native exists but the exact desktop flag combination is unverified, notes beta status and webview as default.
expectations: The answer gives the `native` feature of the `dioxus` crate (`features = ["native"]`) as one route.
The answer gives `dioxus_native::launch(App)` with the `dioxus-native` crate as another route.
The answer says `dx` accepts `--renderer native` and marks the exact combination with a platform flag as unverified.
The answer states that native is beta or opt-in and that webview is the default desktop renderer.
If the answer mentions the Blitz git version of `dioxus-native`, it says to pin a `rev`.

evals.prompt: where do i see current css conformance numbers for blitz and do they apply to my dioxus 0.7.10 app?
evals.expected_output: Points to blitz-wpt-results summary data, explains the pass-rate formula, and warns that the latest numbers are Blitz main (0.3 line), that a 2025-era run is closer to 0.7.x, and that percentages across dates are not comparable.
expectations: The answer points to the `DioxusLabs/blitz-wpt-results` repository (its `summary/` data) as the source.
The answer gives the pass rate as subtests passed divided by subtests run (`scores[3] / scores[2]` or equivalent).
The answer says the latest published numbers reflect Blitz `main` (the 0.3 line), not necessarily the Blitz 0.2 that Dioxus 0.7.10 uses.
The answer says a run near the blitz-dom 0.2.4 release (2025-10-22) is the closer match for a 0.7.x app.
The answer warns that WPT percentages from different dates are not directly comparable because the number of tests run changed.

evals.prompt: is dioxus native faster than the webview renderer? give me rough numbers for startup and frame time so i can put them in a slide
evals.expected_output: Declines to invent numbers; says no benchmark data is available in the sources; suggests measuring on the app's real screens.
expectations: The answer does not give specific startup-time or frame-time figures for either renderer.
The answer states that no benchmark or performance data is available from the sources it used.
The answer recommends measuring the app's real screens on the target hardware.
The answer does not claim that the native renderer is faster, or slower, than the webview renderer as a fact.

evals.prompt: dx serve --renderer native opens a blank white window, nothing in the logs. webview build looks fine. what's wrong
evals.expected_output: Does not assert one root cause; checks dx and dioxus-native/blitz versions; suggests a minimal repro to separate CSS-support problems from others; notes native is beta.
expectations: The answer asks for or checks the output of `dx --version` and of `cargo tree -p dioxus-native` (or `cargo tree -i blitz-dom`).
The answer does not state a single definitive root cause without evidence.
The answer suggests reducing the app to a minimal repro (for example one element of plain text) to separate styling or feature gaps from other causes.
The answer says to compare the CSS features the app uses against the supported-CSS evidence for the pinned Blitz version.
The answer states that the native renderer is beta.

evals.prompt: does dioxus-native support drag and drop and text-overflow: ellipsis right now? we're on 0.7.10
evals.expected_output: Both are unchecked items inside the Blitz 0.3 beta milestone on the roadmap, so neither should be assumed on the 0.7.x line (blitz 0.2); advises a repro.
expectations: The answer says drag and drop is listed as not yet done in the Blitz 0.3 beta milestone and should not be assumed for Dioxus 0.7.x.
The answer says `text-overflow` is listed as not yet done in the Blitz 0.3 beta milestone and should not be assumed for Dioxus 0.7.x.
The answer labels the claims with the roadmap as the evidence source.
The answer recommends confirming with a minimal repro on the pinned version.

evals.prompt: on dioxus-native 0.7.10 my onfocus and onscroll handlers never fire and typing with a japanese IME does nothing. webview build is fine. bug in my code?
evals.expected_output: Reports that in 0.7.10 only mouse move/down/up, click, key down/up/press and input events are converted for Dioxus handlers and IME events are dropped (TODO in source); other kinds are not forwarded (inferred); recommends a repro and notes the roadmap.
expectations: The answer says that in `dioxus-native` 0.7.10 the event handler converts only mouse (move, down, up), click, key (down, up, press) and input events for Dioxus.
The answer says IME events are dropped in 0.7.10 (the source has a TODO for IME handling).
The answer says that focus and scroll events are not forwarded to Dioxus handlers in that release, and labels this as inferred from the source rather than tested.
The answer says the cause is the native renderer rather than the user's code, or recommends confirming with a minimal repro on the pinned version.
